title: Count Collisions on a Road
statement:
`n` cars stand at distinct points of an endless straight road and are numbered `0` to `n - 1` from left to right. Character `directions[i]` says what car `i` does: `'L'` drives left, `'R'` drives right, and `'S'` stays where it is. All moving cars have the same speed.

Collisions are counted this way:

- two cars driving toward each other meet: the count grows by 2;
- a moving car runs into a car that is not moving: the count grows by 1.

Cars involved in a collision stop for good at the spot where it happened (so later cars can run into them). Apart from that, no car ever changes its speed or direction. Return the total count of collisions.
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating the cars step by step is possible but fiddly. Look at who ends up stopped instead. A car that drives left with nothing but left-driving cars ahead of it (a run of `'L'` at the very start) escapes forever, and so does a run of `'R'` at the very end. Every other moving car eventually hits something: between the escaping ends there is always a standing car or a car coming the other way. Each moving car that stops adds exactly 1 (a head-on crash adds 2, one for each car), and standing cars add nothing themselves. So the answer is the number of non-`'S'` cars between the escaping ends.

## Approach

1. Move `left` past the leading `'L'` cars.
2. Move `right` back past the trailing `'R'` cars.
3. Count the characters in `[left, right]` that are not `'S'`; that count is `collisions`.

## Example 1, step by step

`directions = "RLRSLL"`. The first car is `'R'`, so `left` stays at 0; the last car is `'L'`, so `right` stays at 5. Among `R L R S L L` the moving cars are at indices 0, 1, 2, 4 and 5, so `collisions = 5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each pointer and the counting loop pass over the string at most once.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Only the *leading* `'L'` and *trailing* `'R'` cars escape; an `'L'` after any `'R'` or `'S'` will stop.
- A head-on crash is worth 2, which is the same as counting both cars once; do not add an extra point for it.
- Keep the pointers from crossing (`left <= right`), for strings such as `"LLL"` or `"LLRR"` where every car escapes.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left` | first car that is not part of the escaping `'L'` prefix |
| `right` | last car that is not part of the escaping `'R'` suffix |
| `collisions` | moving cars between them, each of which stops |
| `i` | index scanned between `left` and `right` |

narration.2: Start the left pointer at the first car.
narration.4: Leading cars that drive left never meet anything...
narration.7: Trailing cars that drive right escape too.
narration.11: Count the cars that will end up stopped by a collision.
narration.12: Scan every car between the escaping ends.
narration.13: A moving car here must hit something eventually.
narration.14: It contributes exactly one to the count.
narration.17: Every stopped moving car has been counted.
